assumptions: Genuine player0 plus at most 8 map-THING MT_TROOP/MT_POSSESSED, at most 64 map-THING pickups, at most 32 map-THING decorations of the seven E1M1 types and at most 16 map-THING MT_BARREL (DoomEd 2035), every short THING angle, in ten polygon rooms (range, cluster, player_range, monsters, walls, door, fireball, dense64, angles, embedded) built by the M3h9 builder; no Rust expected observations.

Every compiled body, observer, declared adapter and controlled input of M3h2..M3h9 is reused unchanged. Added genuine bodies: PIT_RadiusAttack and P_RadiusAttack (p_map.c, with the globals bombsource, bombspot and bombdamage copied verbatim from p_map.c:1154-1156) and A_Explode (p_enemy.c), which replaces the aborting stub every unlisted action has had since M3d3j. The barrel table of the contract is asserted against the op-0 actor capture of every spawned barrel (type, spawn state, tics 1..6 after the spawn draw, health, radius, height, flags, reaction time, target).

Observers added (no source statement changed): RA after bombdamage is assigned in P_RadiusAttack and a block marker around the unchanged P_BlockThingsIterator call; RC at every return of PIT_RadiusAttack and around the genuine P_CheckSight call (ra_seen returns the value it is given); E action row 5 at A_Explode entry (as A_Scream).

Declared adapters, sanitizer builds only (sanitizer_adapters): p_mobj.c:794 and p_map.c:1221 are rewritten in unsigned arithmetic computing the same 32-bit values; the first is needed (the sanitizer builds report the int product of an octant outside -4..3), the second is declared for robustness (under -std=gnu89 the shift is not reported). The strict build compiles the genuine text, and the three raw traces are byte-identical (sanitizer_comparison).

Controlled inputs: no new input. hit_* (P_DamageMobj(thing, NULL, NULL, amount) between tics) is used only in radius_blocked_by_step (a real shooter thrusts the barrel away from the curb) and fireball_on_dying_barrel (a pistol or fist kill alerts the Imp, whose own fireballs would then reach the live barrel first); attack_at (an Imp S_TROO_ATK1 entry with the player as target) only in fireball_on_dying_barrel; chase_* (target assignment plus see-state entry) for the Zombieman of barrel_infight, the Imp of fireball_kills_barrel and the Imp of embedded_spawns. Scenarios whose outcome depends on the gameplay RNG (fist_kills_barrel and player_killed_by_barrel need a 20-point blow, monster_wakes_mid_walk a failed pain draw, barrel_infight and fireball_kills_barrel a monster that wounds the barrel first) start at a declared seed found by trying every rndtable index; the seed only chooses the starting prndindex, as M_ClearRandom does at 0.

intercept_t intercepts[128] keeps its source size; the harness has aborted before the 129th entry since M3d3 (an observer guard, not a source check: PIT_AddLineIntercepts and PIT_AddThingIntercepts write with no bounds check). The densest trace observed is intercept_heavy_trace (see its case); the Rust-only intercepts129 lane is never run in C.

Bounded original command/weapon stage precedes original thinkers; not complete P_Ticker/PlayerThink/DeathThink or respawn. The reborn request ends player_killed_by_barrel (MG row 2); G_DoReborn is not run.
All M3h1..M3h9 assumptions and adapters apply, including the strict-build retyping of attack-angle int locals; every new row only observes genuine statements.

row_formats.DT: DT,case,op,tmthing,thing,code,flags,result,tmthing z,thing z,thing height: PIT_CheckThing on a thing (flags = thing->flags). code 0: the first flag test passed a thing with none of MF_SOLID|MF_SPECIAL|MF_SHOOTABLE whose box the position check overlaps (printed only when it overlaps; result 1; a flags-0 thing clipping its own position inside P_ThingHeightClip passes itself here, before the self test); code 1: the missile branch met a non-shootable thing and returns !(flags & MF_SOLID) (0 explodes); code 2: the last line of the body for a non-shootable (hence non-special) solid thing returns !(flags & MF_SOLID) = 0 with no height test
row_formats.E: existing; E,case,op,7,actor|-1,sound now also records sfx_noway at the player and the global switch sound of P_ChangeSwitchTexture when buttonlist[0] has no origin
row_formats.F: F,case,0,index,x,y,angle,type,options,owned before,owned after,decision,prndindex: one row per THING record from the P_SpawnMapThing wrapper (decision 0 spawned, 16 options bit 16, 2 skill bit, 1 player start, 11 deathmatch start, 32 MF_NOTDMATCH, 64 nomonsters; prndindex after the record); the index -1 row sums the lump (owned, prndindex, totalkills, totalitems)

row_formats.LE: as M3h7: LE,case,op,kind,id when P_RunThinkers runs a sector thinker, now also kinds 5 door, 6 plat, 7 floor
row_formats.M: as M3h6: M,case,op,attempt,actor,x,y,ok,tmfloorz,tmceilingz,tmdropoffz,floatok,move_failure,subsector,sector,block_line,block_actor; move_failure 1 names the blocking thing (a decoration here), 2 the blocking line (the ML_BLOCKING scroller here)
row_formats.MA: MA,case,op,player,angle,x,y: P_UseLines entry; its P_PathTraverse rows (TR traverser 3, D/B/U/I/TI) carry trace stage 9
row_formats.MB: MB,case,op,slot,line,where,btexture,btimer,soundorg sector (-1 none): a buttonlist slot with a timer, line or sound origin after the op; presentation
row_formats.MC: MC,case,op,0,sector,crunch,floorheight,ceilingheight at P_ChangeSector entry; MC,case,op,1,sector,nofit,floorheight,ceilingheight at its exit

row_formats.MK: MK,case,op,thing,line,index,inclip: PIT_CheckLine is about to store line at spechit[index] for tmthing; inclip 1 inside P_ThingHeightClip. spechit keeps its source size (8)
row_formats.ML: ML,case,op,(line,special)... for every line whose map special is nonzero, after each op (W1/S1 lines read 0 once cleared)

row_formats.MV: MV,case,op,sector,plane,direction,speed,dest,before,after,result: T_MovePlane (plane 0 floor, 1 ceiling; result 0 ok, 1 crushed, 2 pastdest; heights raw)

row_formats.MX: MX,case,op,thing,line,side,special: P_CrossSpecialLine entry from the P_TryMove crossing loop (side = the old side)
row_formats.MY: MY,case,op,thing,line,special: P_CrossSpecialLine exit (0 once a W1 line is cleared)
row_formats.MZ: MZ,case,op,usedown,playerstate,gameaction,secretexit,cmd.buttons of players[0] after each op (gameaction 6 = ga_completed)
row_formats.NS: NS,case,op,attempt,thing,numspechit: printed before every M row (P_TryMove outcome). For a refused move it is the count P_CheckPosition left (what the P_Move failure branch reads next); for an accepted move the crossing loop has already run `while (numspechit--)`, so it reads -1 (the source leaves numspechit at -1 until the next P_CheckPosition)
row_formats.RA: RA,case,op,spot,source,damage,xl,xh,yl,yh,spot x,spot y,spot z,dist: one row per P_RadiusAttack call, printed after bombdamage is assigned (p_map.c:1228): the bomb spot (the exploding thing, A_Explode passes the barrel), the bomb source (thingy->target, -1 for NULL), the damage (128 for A_Explode), the BLOCKMAP window (block columns xl..xh, rows yl..yh, p_map.c:1222-1225), the spot position and the computed `dist` (p_map.c:1221: 8388608 = 128 << 16 on the original targets, the MAXRADIUS term wrapped away). The window is walked y outer, x inner (p_map.c:1230-1232)
row_formats.RC: RC,case,op,thing,block,position,code,dist,damage: one row per PIT_RadiusAttack call, in walk order: the candidate, its BLOCKMAP list (block = y * bmapwidth + x, the blocklinks index the iterator walks), its ordinal among the callbacks of that block (0 = the list head, newest linked; a thing relinked mid-walk changes what follows, p_maputl.c:529-535), and the outcome: 0 not MF_SHOOTABLE (p_map.c:1170), 1 MT_CYBORG/MT_SPIDER (1175), 2 out of range (dist >= bombdamage, 1188), 3 P_CheckSight (thing, bombspot) false (1191), 4 damaged (P_DamageMobj (thing, bombspot, bombsource, bombdamage - dist), 1194; the G rows of that call follow). dist is the floored Chebyshev distance minus the thing radius (p_map.c:1179-1186; -1 for codes 0 and 1), damage is bombdamage - dist for code 4 and 0 otherwise. Printed before the P_DamageMobj call for code 4 and after the P_CheckSight call for codes 3 and 4

row_formats.SF: SF,case,op,id: P_RunThinkers unlinks sector thinker id and calls Z_Free (the harness quarantines it; ids are never reused)

row_formats.TK: as M3h7, plus kind 5 door: id,sector,type,direction,topheight,topcountdown,speed,topwait; kind 6 plat: id,sector,type,status,count,low,high,speed,wait,crush,tag,oldstatus; kind 7 floor: id,sector,type,direction,floordestheight,speed,crush,newspecial,texture; kind 8: id, a sector thinker removed by P_RemoveThinker and not yet unlinked. Mover allocations are zero-filled (declared adapter), so never-written fields print 0
row_formats.XT: XT,case,op,code,shooter,thing,flags: PTR_AimTraverse (code 0) or PTR_ShootTraverse (code 1) skipped a non-shootable thing intercept ("corpse or something") and the trace continues

sanitizer_adapters.reason: ANG45 * q overflows int for quotients outside -4..3 (every angle of 180..359 or below -224, decision F8); the original targets wrap it to q * 0x20000000 mod 2^32, which the unsigned product computes. Needed: without it both sanitizer builds stop at this statement (observed: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 4 * 536870912 cannot be represented in type int).

MAXRADIUS is 32*FRACUNIT without parentheses (p_local.h:51), so (128 + 32*65536) << 16 does not fit in int (undefined behaviour in ISO C99 and later); the original targets keep the low 32 bits, 128 << 16 (decision F5: the window is exactly 3 x 3 blocks), which the unsigned rewrite computes without depending on the language mode. Declared for robustness, not needed by these builds: the harness compiles -std=gnu89 and with the generating compiler neither sanitizer build reports the original statement (GCC checks shift-base only for C99 and later), observed by building both without this adapter.

sanitizer_comparison.rule: --overflow-check rebuilds without -fwrapv under -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow,integer-divide-by-zero,float-cast-overflow and --address-check under -fsanitize=address,undefined (both -fno-sanitize-recover=all), each with the declared sanitizer_adapters applied; each run asserts its raw trace equals the strict -fwrapv trace of the genuine text byte for byte, so raw_trace_sha256 is the digest of all three
